tools.name: run_command

tools.description: Add image/raw files to the library. Folders are scanned recursively for photos; relative paths resolve against the server's working directory. The first imported photo becomes active. Returns the new photo ids.

album.description: Also add to this album id

mode.description: add (default) = reference the files in place; copy = copy them into `destination` (default: the library's Originals/); move = as copy, then each original and its XMP sidecars are removed from the source once the copy is verified and catalogued (duplicates and failures keep their sources; `kept` lists sources left in place and why; undo leaves the moved files at the destination)

onDeleted.description: A file that is in Recently Deleted: restore (default) = bring the photo back with its edits (`restored` lists it; relinked to the file when its own is gone); skip = leave it there (the duplicate is reported with existingDeleted); fresh = delete the trashed record and import the file as a new photo

organize.description: Copy or move: folders inside the destination — date (YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD, default), month (YYYY/YYYY-MM), flat, or a folder template such as {date:%Y}/{date:%Y%m%d} (→ 2026/20260114; the template's / make the levels, tokens as for rename; relative, no ..). Dated by capture time, else the import time

rename.description: Copy or move: file-name template, e.g. {date:%Y%m%d_%H%M%S}_{seq:3} (run_command photo.renameTokens lists the tags); the extension is kept

tools.description: List photos (id, file name, size, rating, flag, edited…). Without filter/sort: the current library view.

tools.description: Set the selection; the active photo (the one develop tools edit) is `active` or the first id.

section.description: Only this section (e.g. light, color, effects, detail)

tools.title: List develop controls

tools.description: The full develop settings JSON of a photo (white balance, light, color, curves, mixer, grading, effects, crop, masks, spots…).

id.description: Photo id (default: the active photo). Reads without changing the selection.

tools.description: Edit a photo (one undo step each for values and settings). `values` sets sliders by control id (see list_controls), e.g. {"light.exposure": 0.7, "light.contrast": 20}. `settings` deep-merges a partial develop-settings JSON (as returned by get_develop).

id.description: Photo id (default: the active photo). Makes that photo active first.

tools.description: Apply a develop preset (ids from cmd_presets_list) to the selection or `ids`, at `amount` percent (0..200, default 100).

tools.title: Apply preset

tools.description: Set the crop of the active photo: `rect` [x0,y0,x1,y1] in normalized coordinates (0..1, origin top-left) of the straightened frame, `angle` in degrees. `reset: true` clears it. Give at least one of them.

id.description: Photo id (default: the active photo). Makes that photo active first.

tools.name: crop
tools.title: Crop / straighten

tools.description: Render a photo with its current develop settings (cropped) and return it as an image so you can look at the result.

format.description: Image encoding (default png; jpeg is smaller)

id.description: Photo id (default: the active photo); selection is unchanged

path.description: Also save the rendered file here

tools.name: render_photo
tools.title: Render photo

tools.description: Render and write photos. Give `path` (one photo; format from the extension unless `format` is set) or `dir` (batch, file names from `naming`).

addToPhotos.description: macOS: after writing the files, add them to Apple Photos (Apple Events to Photos' import; the first time, macOS asks the user to allow LightCraft to control Photos). The outcome is `applePhotos` in the result, the import job: {job, running, requested, album, imported?, ids?, warning?, error?}; headless waits for Photos, the desktop app returns the running job (outcome: command export.photosImports {job}). The files are written either way. An error before exporting on other platforms, or while another import is reserved or running

background.description: Desktop background export (headless exports remain blocking)

bitDepth.description: Bits per channel: PNG 8|16 (default 8), TIFF 8|16|32 (default 16; 32 = linear float with a linear profile), PSD 8|16 (default 16), AVIF 8|10, JPEG XL 8|16; JPEG/WebP are 8-bit

colorSpace.description: Output colour space (default sRGB; AVIF is always sRGB; lossy JPEG XL writes adobeRgb/proPhoto as rec2020). adobeRgb = Adobe RGB (1998) compatible; the embedded ICC profile is generated from the published primaries

destinationMode.description: specificFolder (default) = everything into `dir`; sameAsOriginal = each photo into the folder of its original (+ `subfolder`); a photo with no folder on disk (demo, browser) or whose folder is gone gets an error

dontEnlarge.description: Never upscale past the photo's own size (default true)

format.description: psd = a flat PSD (no layers); rendereddng = Render to DNG, a linear 16-bit float DNG of the rendered photo with the edit baked in; original = the file as is + an XMP sidecar with the edits; dng = raw photos as DNG with the edits embedded

hdr.description: HDR output for photos edited in HDR (develop.hdr): JPEG as an ISO 21496-1 gain map JPEG, AVIF as 10-bit, PNG and JPEG XL as 16-bit Rec. 2020 PQ, 32-bit TIFF with highlights above 1; other formats and SDR edits export as usual

hdrTransfer.description: Transfer curve of HDR AVIF output (default pq): pq = SMPTE ST 2084, hlg = ITU-R BT.2100 hybrid log-gamma

id.description: Photo id (default: the active photo). Makes that photo active first.

ids.description: Photos to export (default: the given/active photo)

jxlEffort.description: JPEG XL encoder effort: normal (default) makes files about a quarter smaller than fast, in about twice the time

jxlLossless.description: JPEG XL: mathematically lossless (quality unused); default false

jxlProgressive.description: JPEG XL: progressive file, a coarse image first (default false)

limitKb.description: JPEG: largest quality that fits this many KB

longEdge.description: Output long edge in px. When no size param is given: 3000; 0 = full size (cropped, native resolution)

percent.description: Output size as a percentage of full size

photosAlbum.description: With addToPhotos: the album to add them to, a top-level Photos album of exactly this name, made when missing (several of that name: nothing is added); default none

ppi.description: Print resolution written into the file (default 240)

resize.description: Full Resize options; alternatively use the size helpers below

watermark.description: Text, or {text, vertical (boolean; defaults to false: upright columns right to left), size (text height as a fraction of the short edge, 0.005..0.5; default 0.035), opacity (0..1; default 0.7), anchor (topLeft|top|topRight|left|center|right|bottomLeft|bottom|bottomRight), insetX (margin from the left or right edge as a fraction of the short edge, 0..0.4; default 0.025), insetY (margin from the top or bottom edge, same units), inset (sets both), rotation (degrees clockwise: 0|90|180|270; default 0; the watermark is sized before it is turned), color [r,g,b] (sRGB 0..255), shadow (boolean), image (path of a graphic drawn instead of the text), imageWidth (fraction of the photo's width, 0.01..1; default 0.2)}. Unknown keys and out-of-range sizes are errors

width.description: Output width in px (with height: fit inside width × height, either orientation)

tools.title: Export photo
